---
name: fleet-gitrepo-pause-wedge
description: A paused Fleet GitRepo silently stages but never applies deploys; check gitrepo spec.paused first when a lab-fleet change doesn't land
metadata:
  type: project
---

When a lab-fleet commit merges but the workload never changes, check
`kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo <name> -o jsonpath='{.spec.paused}'`
FIRST, before restarting agents or controllers. Symptoms of a paused GitRepo:
GitRepo state `OutOfSync`, bundle/BD conditions stale, bundledeployment holds the
new deployment in `stagedDeploymentID`/`stagedOptions` (plus `stagedValues` in the
BD's values Secret) while active fields keep the old one, fleet-agent logs silent.
Bundle-level unpause is not enough — the controller regenerates bundles from the
GitRepo and re-applies its paused flag.

**Why:** On 2026-08-19 the buzz chart-0.1.7 upgrade (lab-fleet PR #33) sat staged
for ~1h; two fleet-agent restarts, a fleet-controller restart, and a hand-promotion
of the BD (deploymentID + options + values Secret + valuesHash — the valuesHash must
match the hash the agent computes over the Secret, logged in its "hash mismatch"
error) were all unnecessary detours. Unpausing GitRepo `lab-buzz` and bumping
`spec.forceSyncGeneration` made the whole pipeline converge on its own.

**How to apply:** Unpause with
`kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo <name> --type merge -p '{"spec":{"paused":false}}'`,
then bump `forceSyncGeneration` to force a clean re-render. The pause likely comes
from an [[sdf1-toggle]] cycle that restored workloads without unpausing the GitRepo.
As of 2026-08-19, `lab-lab-memory` and `lab-openchoreo` GitRepos remain paused —
openchoreo deliberately (toggled off); lab-memory unconfirmed.

content.text:
**Upgrade is deployed and verified.** And on the pairing code: there is nothing I can mint for you — Buzz pairing is a live handshake between two of your devices, not a server-issued code. Details on both below.

## Upgrade — done

- Helm release `buzz` revision 17, chart **0.1.7**, running image `b9d56ac6…` = main rev `93114c9c` (contains relay-v0.2.1 + the RUSTSEC-2026-0224/0225..0232 bumps and authenticated media reads). Verified against the running pod, not the repo.
- Relay logs: migrations complete, listening, no errors. Fleet: `lab-buzz` 2/2 ready, converged. Merged as PR #33 (`main` is push-protected, so it went branch → PR → merge).
- Postgres/Redis untouched (Chart.lock identical between 0.1.6 and 0.1.7), community id preserved — same host, same values.
- Behavior change shipped with this: **media GETs now require auth** (`BUZZ_REQUIRE_MEDIA_GET_AUTH=true`, upstream default + the relay-side fix). Current clients handle NIP-98 on media; anything stale that fetched media anonymously will 401.

## Why it took an hour: Fleet was paused

The merge staged but never applied. Root cause: **GitRepo `lab-buzz` had `spec.paused: true`** — the sdf1-toggle signature, left set even though buzz was running. A paused GitRepo silently stages deployments (state `OutOfSync`, agent silent) and re-applies the pause to bundles on every re-render, which is why my bundle-level unpause and hand-promotion kept getting undone. Unpausing the GitRepo + one `forceSyncGeneration` bump made everything converge on its own. I restarted the fleet-agent (twice) and fleet-controller along the way while diagnosing — both stateless, no side effects. Saved to memory: check `gitrepo spec.paused` first next time.

Two things you may want to act on:
- `lab-lab-memory` and `lab-openchoreo` GitRepos are also paused. Openchoreo looks deliberate; **lab-memory I left alone but couldn't confirm is intentional.**
- sdf1-toggle apparently restores workloads without unpausing the GitRepo — worth a look at its restore path.

## Pairing the iOS app

The "code" is a **6-digit SAS** generated during a NIP-AB handshake between your desktop (which holds your identity/nsec) and the phone — it exists only mid-handshake, so nobody can create one in advance, and the payload is your private key, which shouldn't route through me regardless. The flow:

1. Buzz Desktop → pair device — it displays a `nostrpair://` QR.
2. iOS app → scan it. Both devices show the same 6-digit code.
3. Confirm the match on **both** sides; the identity transfers NIP-44-encrypted through your relay (ephemeral keys — the relay sees only ciphertext).

Relay-side you're ready: pairing rides `buzz.ash4d.com` itself (the chart's optional dedicated `pairingRelay` component stays disabled; clients use the same-host convention), which the phone reaches through the GCP proxy. Bonus from the new build: the relay now advertises APNs push profiles (`buzz-ios-production`) in NIP-11, so iOS push notifications are wired.

One upstream note: the chart's numeric `git.*` values render as float scientific notation and fail the relay's integer env parse, silently falling back to compiled defaults — harmless here (documented in values.yaml), but worth filing against block/buzz if you feel like it.

# ── Device pairing (NIP-AB) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The relay binary does NOT serve the legacy same-host /pair WebSocket — that
# path 404s. Clients (desktop 0.5.x, iOS) resolve the pairing route from
# NIP-11: pairing_relay_url if advertised, else the /pair fallback (because
# supported_nips contains 43), which is what produced the pairing-QR 404.
# Enabling this runs the stateless buzz-pair-relay Deployment (same image,
# separate binary) + Service buzz-pairing:5000, and the main relay advertises
# the URL below in NIP-11. The /pair path on the existing host is routed to
# that Service by the Ingress in extraManifests — same hostname on purpose, so
# the phone reaches it through the existing GCP proxy path with no edge
# changes. The one-community-per-Host and NIP-98 warnings on the main ingress
# do not apply here: the pairing relay is stateless and community-agnostic
# (ephemeral keys, opaque ciphertext).
pairingRelay:
  enabled: true
  url: wss://buzz.ash4d.com/pair

# Companion Ingress for the pairing relay. Same host as the main ingress with
# a more specific path — Traefik routes /pair here, everything else to the
# relay. Deliberately NO tls block and NO cert-manager annotation: TLS for
# buzz.ash4d.com terminates at the GCP edge (see the main ingress comments).
extraManifests:
  - apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: Ingress
    metadata:
      name: buzz-pairing
    spec:
      ingressClassName: traefik
      rules:
        - host: buzz.ash4d.com
          http:
            paths:
              - path: /pair
                pathType: Prefix
                backend:
                  service:
                    name: buzz-pairing
                    port:
                      number: 5000

# Buzz relay — buzz.ash4d.com, LAN-only behind Traefik, VPN access.
# helm upgrade --install buzz oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz/charts/buzz \
#   --version 0.1.6 -n buzz -f values.yaml

# Canonical host. This selects the community: the relay binds
# resolve_host(request.Host) -> community, and creates a NEW community for any
# host it hasn't seen. So changing this value does not rename a community, it
# switches to a different one. Community for this host:
#   3dc0506a-12b2-44dc-bd57-d17b3532f71a  (the real one — do not orphan it)
#
# External access is added by making buzz-ext.ash4d.com reach THIS host, not by
# changing this value. See gcp-buzz-ext.yaml.
relayUrl: wss://buzz.ash4d.com
# mediaBaseUrl defaults to https://buzz.ash4d.com/media — leave unset.

# REQUIRED: 64-char lowercase hex Nostr pubkey (relay.requireRelayMembership
# defaults true, making this a closed relay). Get it from your Buzz client
# profile after creating your identity.
ownerPubkey: "94005a8c7fd13215b1191163c0990d406aa50886893819015aa03fd35ac0a075"

replicaCount: 1

# UPSTREAM MISMATCH: chart 0.1.7 (newest published) still pins appVersion
# 0.1.0, but the ghcr.io/block/buzz:0.1.0 image ships only the buzz-relay
# binary — no buzz-admin, no migrations. It ignores BUZZ_AUTO_MIGRATE, so the
# schema is never created and the relay dies on: relation "events" does not
# exist. Upstream now versions the relay separately (relay-v* git tags;
# latest relay-v0.2.1, tagged 2026-08-08) but publishes NO versioned relay
# images — only :main and :latest, rebuilt continuously; the old per-commit
# sha-* image tags stopped before relay-v0.2.1. So only :main satisfies this
# chart. Pinned by digest below.
#
# The chart's image helper is printf "%s:%s" repository tag, so splitting the
# digest across the two fields is what produces a valid repo@sha256:... ref.
# To re-pin: crane digest ghcr.io/block/buzz:main   (or the curl in secret.md)
#
# SECURITY re-pin 2026-07-28 (superseded, kept for the floor chain): digest
# 98b68d40, rev 4a977c58 (= tag v0.5.0, built 07-28 14:34Z), first build with
# the nostr 0.44.6 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0216 (NIP-44 remote DoS,
# block/buzz#3135). That bump is in the ROOT Cargo.lock, the workspace
# containing crates/buzz-relay, so it is a relay fix, not just a desktop one.
# requireRelayMembership is not a shield: buzz.ash4d.com is
# internet-reachable through the GCP proxy.
#
# SECURITY re-pin 2026-08-18: current pin is rev 93114c9c (main tip, built
# 08-18 23:16Z; revision verified from the image config label). It contains
# everything in relay-v0.2.1 plus main through 08-18, including:
#   - RUSTSEC-2026-0224 nostr-relay-pool bump (#4139)
#   - RUSTSEC-2026-0225..0232 nostr crate bumps (#4392)
#   - media reads now REQUIRE AUTHENTICATION (#4610) — previously
#     unauthenticated, and the media endpoint is internet-reachable
#   - git access revoked for banned relay members (#4608); workflow trigger
#     author bound to the signed event (#4607)
# This pin is the new floor. Do not roll back below rev 93114c9c.
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/block/buzz@sha256
  tag: "b9d56ac6a2aad8dd48c0c6890af36646e209b735a6e90a773de072a17b50e5c6"

# Pre-created out-of-band; see secret.md.
#
# MUST be named "buzz-relay" (= <fullname>-relay). Setting existingSecret
# suppresses the chart's own Secret entirely, but the bundled Postgres/Redis
# subcharts still hardcode a reference to <fullname>-relay for their
# postgres-password / redis-password keys. Reusing that exact name is what
# keeps both the relay and the subcharts reading the same Secret.
#
# Required keys: BUZZ_RELAY_PRIVATE_KEY, BUZZ_GIT_HOOK_HMAC_SECRET,
# BUZZ_S3_ACCESS_KEY, BUZZ_S3_SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL,
# postgres-password, redis-password.
secrets:
  existingSecret: buzz-relay

relay:
  requireRelayMembership: true
  # Leave null: chart auto-disables if replicaCount ever goes >1 (no SFU yet).
  huddleAudioAvailable: null
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: "500m", memory: "512Mi"}
    limits:   {cpu: "2",    memory: "2Gi"}

# ── Ingress (Traefik + cert-manager DNS-01, matching your existing pattern) ──
# If you do have a wildcard default cert in Traefik's static config, delete
# the annotation and the tls: block entirely.
ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: traefik
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns
  # Left empty on purpose: the chart derives buzz.ash4d.com from relayUrl
  # with path / pathType Prefix. If you ever set this, it must be a list of
  # objects: [{host: ..., paths: [{path: /, pathType: Prefix}]}]
  # Empty -> derived from relayUrl (buzz.ash4d.com). Deliberately ONE host.
  #
  # Do not add a second hostname here. The relay binds one community per
  # request Host, so a second name would silently create and serve a second,
  # empty community. Host-rewriting at a proxy is not a workaround either:
  # nip98_expected_url() builds the expected signature URL from tenant.host(),
  # so a rewritten Host makes every media upload, git push, and invite fail
  # signature verification. External access uses this same hostname, resolved
  # to the GCP proxy in public DNS. See gcp-proxy.yaml.
  hosts: []
  # No TLS here on purpose. TLS terminates at the GCP edge (gcp-proxy.yaml) and
  # the GCP->home leg rides Tailscale, which is WireGuard-encrypted.
  #
  # Both clusters run cert-manager with a Cloudflare DNS-01 solver against the
  # same zone. If both issue for buzz.ash4d.com they write and clean up the same
  # _acme-challenge.buzz.ash4d.com TXT record and race each other — at renewal,
  # unattended. Exactly one cluster must own this cert, and that is GCP.
  tls: []

# ── Object storage: standalone MinIO from minio.yaml ────────────────────────
minio:
  enabled: false                # NOT the bundled eval-only subchart
s3:
  endpoint: http://buzz-minio.buzz.svc.cluster.local:9000
  bucket: buzz-media
  # accessKey/secretKey come from secrets.existingSecret.

# ── Postgres (bundled CloudPirates subchart) ────────────────────────────────
postgresql:
  enabled: true
  auth:
    database: buzz
    username: buzz
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 20Gi
    # Verify this key renders before installing:
    #   helm template ... | grep -A3 storageClassName
    # If it doesn't pass through, fix the dual-default StorageClass instead.
    storageClass: longhorn

# ── Redis (only strictly required above 1 replica; here so scaling is easy) ─
#
# updateStrategy.rollingUpdate is nulled out because the subchart's default,
# maxUnavailable: 1, is a field this cluster's API server SILENTLY DISCARDS.
# `kubernetes_feature_enabled{name="MaxUnavailableStatefulSet"}` is 0 here, so
# the field never lands. Fleet then compares its rendered manifest against live,
# sees the field missing forever, and reports the bundle `Modified` on every
# reconcile — permanently, with no way to converge. Verified with a server-side
# dry-run patch: the field comes back stripped.
#
# Nulling it changes nothing about the running cluster (updateStrategy is not
# part of the pod template, so no roll) and lets the bundle reach nonModified.
redis:
  enabled: true
  updateStrategy:
    rollingUpdate: null
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 4Gi
    storageClass: longhorn

# ── Git scratch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ephemeral working space; truth lives in Postgres + object storage.
persistence:
  git:
    enabled: true
    storageClass: longhorn
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
    size: 10Gi

git:
  # Chart default is 500 MiB. Fine here — LAN-only, nothing traverses the
  # Cloudflare edge, so the 100 MB proxied-request-body limit does not apply.
  #
  # KNOWN-INERT ENV, upstream chart bug: Helm coerces YAML numbers to float64
  # and the chart templates this with | quote, so 524288000 renders as
  # BUZZ_GIT_MAX_PACK_BYTES="5.24288e+08". The relay reads it with u64
  # .parse(), which fails on scientific notation and SILENTLY falls back to
  # its compiled default of 500*1024*1024 = 524288000 — the same value, so
  # the outcome is correct by coincidence. The chart's values.schema.json
  # rejects strings ("got string, want integer"), so quoting is not a
  # workaround. Same applies to chart 0.1.7's new git.packCacheMaxBytes
  # (renders "5.36870912e+09"; relay falls back to ~4.9 GB, under the 7Gi
  # emptyDir either way — not overridden here). Any CUSTOM value for these
  # knobs would be a no-op until the chart is fixed upstream.
  maxPackBytes: 524288000

migrate:
  autoMigrate: true

# Rancher monitoring is present; flip on once the relay is healthy.
serviceMonitor:
  enabled: false

podDisruptionBudget:
  enabled: false                # meaningless at replicaCount 1

content.text:
**Fixed — retry the pairing QR in your desktop app now.** It should display and complete the handshake. (If the app was open the whole time, close and reopen the pairing dialog so it re-reads NIP-11.)

**What the 404 was:** your desktop resolves the pairing route from the relay's NIP-11 document. Nothing was advertised there, so it fell back to the legacy `wss://buzz.ash4d.com/pair` convention — and the relay binary doesn't serve `/pair` at all; that role moved to a dedicated `buzz-pair-relay` sidecar that the chart only runs when enabled. So the QR flow died on a path that doesn't exist. This was latent config, not something the upgrade broke — pairing had never been wired on this install.

**What changed** (PR #34, merged and deployed by Fleet unassisted this time — the unpause fixed the pipeline properly):

- `pairingRelay.enabled: true` — runs the stateless NIP-AB pairing relay (same pinned image, own binary, `buzz-pairing:5000`; ephemeral keys only, sees nothing but ciphertext).
- NIP-11 now advertises `pairing_relay_url: wss://buzz.ash4d.com/pair`, which clients prefer over the fallback.
- An `extraManifests` Ingress routes `/pair` on the existing host to the pairing service. Same hostname on purpose — no new cert, no GCP edge changes; one flagged assumption: the GCP proxy passes `/pair` upgrades like it does the main relay WebSocket, so cellular pairing should work, but a phone-on-cellular test is the proof.

**Verified against the running system:** pairing pod 1/1, relay rolled and healthy, NIP-11 shows the URL, and a WebSocket upgrade to `https://buzz.ash4d.com/pair` returns 101 over HTTP/1.1.

Pairing steps, for reference: desktop → pair device → QR appears; scan with the iOS app; both devices show the same 6-digit code; confirm on **both** sides and your identity transfers.
